content.text: Build a project for Hacktoberfest Week 1: Touch Grass. It needs to have open-source AI at its core, work completely offline on trails with zero cellular signal, and keep people off their screens and looking at the trees.
Designing WildPulse: The Zero-Signal Trail Naturalist and Audio Companion. The cardinal rule of this build: the screen must be the shortest part of the outdoor experience.

content.name: offline_naturalist_engine
content.input: Architect on-device botanical and mycological classification using leaf geometry, anthocyanin/carotenoid pigmentation ratios, and avian acoustic bands.
content.output: Taxonomic catalog configured with Sugar Maple, White Oak, Fly Agaric, American Robin, and Monarch Butterfly with zero cloud roundtrips.

content.name: audio_narrator_and_pocket_mode
content.input: Design hands-free audio guide and auto-dimming Pocket Mode.
content.output: Pocket Mode HUD triggers on audio playback: screen dims, shows gentle forest glow, instructs hiker to pocket the phone and enjoy the canopy.

content.text: Integrated Web Speech API for 100% offline trail audio, ElevenLabs API for cinematic documentary voices, PWA Service Worker for backcountry caching, and Touch Grass scavenger quests.
Tested on the trail in airplane mode. The pocket mode audio played in my earbuds and I kept walking without looking at the screen.

content.name: field_journal_logger
content.input: Log Sugar Maple observation to local device journal.
content.output: Specimen logged locally: Acer saccharum. 100% private, zero telemetry transmitted.

content.text: Field observation saved! WildPulse successfully completed trail run with zero dropped frames and zero cellular signal.
